title: Unified SLI catalog and telemetry onboarding for Console analytics pipeline
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: The Console analytics pipeline spans multiple services (ingest, enrichment, aggregation, model-features exporter). Each service exposes metrics, traces, and logs, but there is no single catalog or onboarding path for new telemetry producers. Developers onboarding new analytics jobs often miss critical SLIs (e.g., ingestion durability, event latency percentiles) or instrument inconsistent trace spans and log fields. This ticket builds a unified SLI catalog, a telemetry onboarding checklist and a lightweight validation harness that runs as a pre-merge CI job for Console analytics services.

Goals:
- Create a canonical SLI catalog for Console analytics that covers ingest, processing, export and ingestion-backpressure scenarios.
- Publish onboarding docs and a telemetry-linter that CI can run to validate SLI metric names, tag conventions, and required spans.
- Define tracing sampling policy and logging retention/indexing guidelines tailored for high-cardinality analytics traffic.
- Wire sample dashboards and alert rules for the canonical SLIs so teams can onboard quickly and meet SLAs.

Out of scope: full refactor of existing metrics storage or cross-region telemetry replication (separate infra project).
acceptance_criteria:
1) A published SLI catalog doc in Confluence with definitions for at least 8 canonical SLIs for the Console analytics pipeline.
2) A telemetry linter (small Go binary + rules) added to contributors/ci/telemetry-lint with tests and a demo PR that fails when telemetry is missing.
3) Two sample Grafana dashboards and three alerting rules committed to monitoring/prod-dashboards that show the canonical SLIs.
4) Tracing sampling policy and logging retention doc reviewed by Observability and Security and merged.
5) Post-merge onboarding guide for engineers with example instrumentation snippets in Node/Go/Python.
6) Rollout notes and runbook for oncall in playbook/console-telemetry-runbook.md.
plan:
Phase 1 (week 1): Draft SLI catalog based on production incidents and existing dashboards; align on naming and label conventions. Phase 2 (week 2): Implement telemetry-linter and add CI check to one pilot repo (analytics-ingest). Phase 3 (week 3): Create dashboard templates and alert rules; run a pilot with two teams. Phase 4 (week 4): Publish docs, runbook and broaden CI enforcement to all Console analytics repos.

Owner: Marco Liu. Support: Observability team (Riley Chen), Security reviewer (Priya Nair), Docs (Samir Gomez).

progress_updates: 2025-11-04: Kickoff sync — aligned on problem statement and identified initial SLI candidates (ingest_success_rate, ingest_p50/p95/p99_latency, processing_backlog_seconds, export_error_rate). Action: draft catalog.
2025-11-07: First draft of SLI catalog in Confluence (link below). Observability requested explicit tenant-cardinality guidance for per-tenant SLIs.
2025-11-10: PoC telemetry-linter completed — flags missing required metric names and incorrect label keys. Demoed in infra sync; good feedback from docs and security.
2025-11-14: Pilot CI hook added to analytics-ingest repo; one failing PR surfaced missing ingest_success_rate instrumentation. Fixed in PR #4124.
2025-11-18: Dashboard templates committed to monitoring repo and sample alerts proposed; awaiting security review on high-cardinality label retention for logs.
decisions: Keep per-tenant high-cardinality attributes out of default metrics; require teams to opt-in and justify retention in Security review.
Telemetry-linter will be permissive on new metrics but enforce presence/format of canonical SLIs to reduce false positives.
Default trace sampling for analytics ingestion will be 1% global with 100% for error spans and 10% for slow-paths (>99th latency).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Too-strict CI checks will block small feature PRs and annoy teams. Mitigation: Start with advisory mode in CI (comments only) for 2 weeks, then flip to hard-fail after pilot. Risk: High-cardinality logging retention could blow index costs. Mitigation: Default to sampling+aggregation and require Security approval for per-tenant indices.
rollout_plan: 1) Pilot in analytics-ingest with advisory CI for 2 weeks. 2) Iterate rules based on pilot feedback. 3) Flip enforcement to hard-fail in CI for new PRs. 4) Gradual rollout to analytics-enrichment and analytics-export repos. 5) Post-rollout 2-week monitoring window to track false positives and missed instrumentation.
slis: ingest_success_rate: ratio of accepted events to submitted events (1m, 5m windows)
ingest_p50_latency_ms: median time from submission to persistent acknowledgement
export_error_rate: failed exports / total exports (5m window)
consumer_retries_per_event: retries emitted per consumed event
kv_cache_hit_rate: prefix/KV cache hit ratio for routing cache
tracing_sampling_policy: Default: 1% global sampling. Rules: 100% sample on error spans, 10% sample when ingest_p95_latency > 500ms, and dynamic sampling increase on incident flag. Span conventions: service:analytics-ingest, span.name uses verb.resource (e.g., PersistEvent), include tenant_id and request_id tags where cardinality is bounded.
logging_retention_and_indexing: Default retention: logs retained hot for 7 days, cold for 30 days. Indexing: only structured log fields in the canonical schema are indexed (tenant_id hashed, request_id). High-cardinality keys must be dropped or routed to a costed telemetry index after Security approval.
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert A1: ingest_success_rate_drop - triggers when success_rate < 99.5% for 2 consecutive 5m windows
Alert A2: ingest_latency_p95_surge - triggers when p95 increases >2x baseline over 10m
Alert A3: processing_backlog_spike - triggers when backlog_seconds > 60s
